# PRD

- **Spec:** `01_rebuild_worktree` (id `01`, name `rebuild_worktree`)
- **Title:** Run Carry-Patch Rebuilds in a Detached Worktree
- **Status:** active
- **Schema version:** 3
- **Created:** 2026-10-01T07:34:32.481635Z
- **Source:** https://github.com/agent-fox-dev/hub/issues/34
- **Intent hash:** `13620b0887116dd73d752e2a5243199880048a495e509b68a7d1a67684bb797b`

## Intent

A carry-patch rebuild applies patch branches onto the upstream base to produce the integration branch. Branches are refs and need no working tree, but cherry-pick and merge do, and today the rebuild borrows the workspace's single shared trunk checkout for them and holds the per-workspace lock for the whole run. This spec moves patch application into a detached, per-run `git worktree` that shares the trunk's objects, refs, configuration and rerere cache but has its own HEAD, index and files. After the change a rebuild never moves or modifies the trunk checkout, leaves nothing behind in the trunk if it crashes, and holds the workspace lock only for the steps that really conflict with other operations. The rebuild algorithm (strategy, fail modes, merge detection, soft deletion, position compaction, progress, rollback) and the public API keep their current meaning.

## Goals

- A rebuild never changes the trunk's HEAD, index or working-tree files. After a successful run, a fail-fast conflict, a continue-mode conflict or a cancelled run, `git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain` and the contents of a sample file in the trunk are identical to what they were before. The two exceptions are the one-time `_rebuild_temp` migration and the integration-branch-checked-out case (Requirement 2).
- Patches are applied in a worktree created for the run at `<workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>` and removed when the run ends, on every exit path. The `_rebuild_temp` branch is no longer created.
- The workspace lock (`wslock`) is held only for (a) the upstream fetch and base resolution and (b) the final integration-ref update, patch bookkeeping and optional push to `origin`. During patch application, `POST /sync`, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase, merge jobs and the post-push working-tree reset all proceed.
- Archive and reclone answer `409 workspace_busy` for the whole run, because they delete the directory the worktree lives in. They are guarded by a new per-workspace rebuild-active flag in `internal/wslock`.
- The patch tips applied by a run are fixed when it starts (resolved to SHAs). If a patch branch or the upstream base moved during the run, a follow-up rebuild is enqueued instead of the change being lost.
- Stale rebuild worktrees left by a crash are removed before the next rebuild of that workspace and once at hub startup, without touching the trunk.
- Rerere keeps working: resolutions recorded in one rebuild replay in the next, and `GET /rerere` and `DELETE /rerere/*` read and forget the same `rr-cache`.
- Endpoints, response shapes, job records and existing audit events are unchanged, apart from one additive field `patch_results[].source_sha` and one new audit event `hub.rebuild.followup`. Only the documented `409 workspace_busy` behaviour narrows.

## Non-goals

- **Replacing the git CLI with go-git for the rebuild.** go-git v5.19.1 reportedly has no linked-worktree, cherry-pick, non-FF merge or rerere support (see Verified External API). The rebuild keeps using `gitcmd.GitRunner`. Existing go-git use (fetch, push, post-push reset, sync fast-forward, `DefaultPushIntegrationFunc`) is neither extended nor removed.
- **Changing where patch branches live** (hub-local versus mirrored to the fork; see `docs/adr/01-choose-the-authority-for-patch-branches.md`). This spec fetches and pushes no patch branch.
- **Moving merge jobs, sync or the push hook into worktrees.** They keep using the trunk. The `rebuild/<job id>` layout leaves room for a later `merge/<job id>`.
- **Guarding `DELETE /workspaces/:slug`.** It requires an archived workspace, and archive is refused while a rebuild is active. The residual race (a rebuild that starts on an archived workspace whose clone was retained) ends in a failed rebuild, not corruption.
- **Concurrent rebuilds of one workspace.** The queue serialises by group key and dedups on `(type, key)`. The guard also rejects a second rebuild of the same workspace.
- **Multi-replica hubs.** `wslock` is in-process and stays so.
- **Sparse or partial checkouts** of the worktree.
- **Changing the rebuild algorithm** (strategy selection, fail modes, merge detection, soft deletion, compaction, progress, rollback semantics).
- **Pinning the trunk's checkout to the workspace branch.** Today it is wherever the last merge job or push left it; that stays so.
- **Following up on a retryable failure.** A retried job re-snapshots on its own.

## Background

Every workspace is a non-bare clone at `<workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk`, shared by the git smart HTTP server, sync, merge jobs, rollback, rerere forget and rebuilds. `internal/wslock` (a per-slug `sync.Mutex` map offering `Lock` for jobs and `TryLock` for handlers) keeps them apart.

What the code does today (`internal/carrypatch/rebuild_executor.go`, `HandleRebuildJob`):

- Takes `wslock.Lock(slug)` before the upstream fetch and holds it to the end, including the DB bookkeeping and the optional `PushIntegration` to `origin`.
- Records the trunk's checkout (`currentCheckout`), runs `preflightCleanup` (`cherry-pick/merge/rebase --abort` plus `HardReset("HEAD")`), then `checkout -B _rebuild_temp <base>`.
- Cherry-picks (`applyRebasePatch`: `git log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick <base>...<branch>`) or merges (`applyMergePatch`: `MergeNoFF(branchName)`) in the trunk, using `git rerere` through `handleConflictWithRerere`.
- Force-updates the integration branch with `branch -f <integration> HEAD`, then `restoreCheckout` (`checkout --force`) and `branch -D _rebuild_temp`.
- Cleanup runs with the job context. On cancellation that context is already dead and `GitRunner.runWithExitCode` returns `ctx.Err()` without starting git, so cleanup silently does nothing. This is why `preflightCleanup` exists.

Other facts the design depends on:

- Handlers that `TryLock`: `internal/workspace/handlers.go` (archive), `reclone_handler.go`, `sync_handler.go`, `internal/carrypatch/sync_handlers.go` (carry-patch sync), `rerere_handlers.go`, `api.go` (rollback), `internal/merge/api.go`. The merge job uses blocking `Lock`. `internal/gitserver/handlers.go` `updateHeadSHA` does `TryLock` and skips the go-git hard reset when the lock is held.
- Rollback runs `git branch -f <integration> <previous sha>`.
- The jobs queue (`internal/jobqueue/jobqueue.go`) dedups `Enqueue` on `(type, key)` for jobs in status `queued` or `running`. `claimAndExecute` will not start a queued job while another job of the same type and group key is running. `Job` carries `GroupKey`; the running job's ID is available via `jobqueue.JobIDFromContext`.
- `carrypatch.GitRunner` is an interface (`Run`, `CherryPick`, `MergeNoFF`, `MergeTree`, `IsAncestor`, `Cherry`, `HardReset`) implemented in production by `GitRunnerAdapter` over `*gitcmd.GitRunner` (`wire.go`) and in tests by `mockGitRunner` (`testhelpers_test.go`). `RebuildHandler.NewGitRunner(repoPath)` builds one; `gitcmd.New` requires the directory to exist and enforces git ≥ 2.38.
- The rerere handlers read `<trunk>/.git/rr-cache` and `<trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR` directly.
- `carryPatchPostCloneSetup` (`internal/workspace/queue.go`) already enables rerere in repository config at clone time.
- `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md` ("Rebuild algorithm", about line 810) and `docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md` (lines about 455 and 557) describe `_rebuild_temp`. `docs/api.md` ("Workspace Lock", error table, per-endpoint 409 rows) and `docs/openapi.yaml` describe `workspace_busy`. The only existing ADR is `docs/adr/01-...`.

Three problems in the originating proposal were found by reading the code, and the requirements below handle them:

1. A follow-up rebuild enqueued from inside the running rebuild is rejected by the `(type, key)` dedup, because the running job is itself `running`. The queue needs a way to ignore the caller.
2. The proposal says a sync that advances upstream during a rebuild is harmless because "the next scheduled sync catches up". It does not. Carry-patch sync writes `upstream_head_sha` and only enqueues a rebuild when upstream advanced relative to that stored value, so after a sync that ran during a rebuild the next sync sees no change and never rebuilds. Today this cannot happen because the sync gets 409 and records nothing. Narrowing the lock would turn that into a silently lost rebuild unless the rebuild checks for upstream drift itself.
3. `git branch -f` refuses to move a branch that is checked out in any worktree, including the trunk, so the final ref update must use `update-ref`.

## Requirements

### 1. Worktree lifecycle

For each run the rebuild creates a detached worktree with a typed `WorktreeAdd` call that runs `git worktree add --detach <path> <upstream base sha>` in the trunk. `<path>` is `<workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>`. It must be made absolute (`filepath.Abs`), because git resolves a relative path against the runner's working directory, which is the trunk. When the context carries no job ID (unit tests) a random ID is used. When `WorkspaceRoot` is empty the path is derived from the same parent as the trunk path, so the existing unit tests that use a fake runner keep working.

A second `GitRunner` is built for the worktree with `h.NewGitRunner(worktreePath)`, after the directory exists. All patch application runs through it: `log`, `rev-parse`, cherry-pick, merge, `rerere`, `diff --diff-filter=U`, `commit --no-edit`, `reset --hard` (continue-mode rollback to the pre-patch HEAD) and reading the worktree HEAD. The trunk runner is used only for fetch-adjacent reads, `config`, worktree add/remove/prune, the `_rebuild_temp` migration (Requirement 2) and the final ref update.

The worktree is removed on every exit path: success, conflict, transient error, panic-free early return and cancellation. Removal is typed `WorktreeRemove` (`git worktree remove --force <path>`) followed by `WorktreePrune` (`git worktree prune`). If `worktree remove` fails, the rebuild falls back to `os.RemoveAll(path)` then prune. Removal is best-effort, is logged on failure, and never changes the job outcome. Removal and any other cleanup run with a context derived from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` and a bounded timeout (for example two minutes), so they still work after the job context is cancelled.

The three typed methods are added to `gitcmd.GitRunner`, to the `carrypatch.GitRunner` interface, to `GitRunnerAdapter` and to `mockGitRunner`. They are the only place worktree commands are spelled, so a later move to go-git touches one adapter. `MergeNoFF` gains a message parameter (`MergeNoFF(ctx, ref, message string) error`; an empty message keeps git's default) so Requirement 6 can merge a SHA while naming the branch.

Verification: a real-repository integration test runs a rebuild and asserts the worktree directory is gone and `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk after success, conflict, transient failure and cancellation.

### 2. The trunk is not touched

During a rebuild the trunk runner runs no `checkout`, `reset`, `cherry-pick`, `merge` or `rebase`. `currentCheckout`, `restoreCheckout` and `preflightCleanup` are deleted.

**Final ref update.** The integration branch is force-updated from the worktree's final HEAD SHA with `git update-ref refs/heads/<integration> <sha>` (the existing `UpdateRef` method). It never uses `branch -f` (which refuses checked-out branches) and never checks the integration branch out. The previous value is read with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration>` immediately before the update, under the lock, and recorded as `previous_integration_head_sha`; an absent branch leaves it empty as today.

**Exception A, integration branch checked out in the trunk.** If, under the final lock, the trunk's HEAD is the symbolic ref of the integration branch (possible after a merge job or a hub push), moving the ref would leave the trunk's index and files at the old commit. In that case, and only then, the rebuild runs `reset --hard HEAD` in the trunk after the ref update so the checkout matches the new tip, which is what the old restore step achieved. This is logged at info level.

**Exception B, one-time `_rebuild_temp` migration.** Under the first lock phase, if a local `refs/heads/_rebuild_temp` exists (left by a pre-upgrade crash or an interrupted pre-upgrade run), the rebuild removes it and logs that it did so. If the trunk's HEAD is on that branch, it first aborts any in-progress cherry-pick, merge or rebase (best-effort) and moves HEAD with `checkout --force <branch>`, where `<branch>` is the workspace's configured branch (`workspaceBranch`) if it exists as a local branch, else the short name of `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` if that exists locally, else `checkout --detach --force` with a warning. After migration the branch is never created again.

Verification: the test in Requirement 1 compares trunk HEAD, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --porcelain` and a sample file before and after a successful run, a fail-fast conflict, a continue-mode conflict and a cancelled run. Separate tests cover Exception A and Exception B.

### 3. Rerere across worktrees

`rerere.enabled=true` and `rerere.autoupdate=true` are repository-level and are set with the trunk runner before the worktree is created, as the rebuild does today. The hub does not enable `extensions.worktreeConfig`. `rr-cache` lives in the common git directory, so replay and recording in the worktree use the same cache the rerere endpoints read. `MERGE_RR` is per-worktree in git; it is only populated while a conflict is in progress and the worktree is discarded afterwards, so the endpoints' use of `<trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR` is unaffected in practice. The implementation must not assume any of this without the test below.

Verification: an integration test records a rerere resolution in one rebuild's worktree, runs a second rebuild and asserts the resolution is replayed with no conflict, and that `GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere` lists the entry and `DELETE` forgets it.

### 4. Lock phases

The run proceeds in this order:

1. Resolve upstream credentials (as today; failure is a retryable `TransientError`).
2. `wslock.Lock(slug)` (blocking, as today). Under it, set the rebuild-active guard (Requirement 5).
3. **Phase one, under the lock:** upstream fetch, trunk runner creation, upstream base resolution (`resolveUpstreamBase`), the `_rebuild_temp` migration, stale worktree cleanup (Requirement 8), rerere config. Then unlock.
4. Create the worktree, list patches, snapshot tips (Requirement 6), apply patches. **No lock held.**
5. **Phase two, re-acquire `wslock.Lock(slug)`:** read the previous integration head, update the integration ref (with Exception A), soft-delete `merged_upstream` patches, compact positions, optional `PushIntegration` to `origin`. Unlock.
6. Remove the worktree, run the stale-input check (Requirement 7), emit `hub.rebuild.complete`, clear the guard, return.

The lock is released on every early return in phase one and phase two. Patch application and worktree creation and removal never run under the lock.

During step 4, `POST /sync`, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase and merge jobs proceed as if no rebuild were running. A rollback during step 4 is legitimate: the rebuild's later `update-ref` overwrites it, and `previous_integration_head_sha` reflects the value at phase two. Because rollback and the rebuild's final update both take the lock, they cannot interleave writes to the integration branch. A `hub.rebuild.fail` event is still emitted on any error return.

If the hub is waiting on `Lock` while archive or reclone run and the workspace is removed, the fetch then fails and the job is retried by the queue under its existing retry policy; no new behaviour is added.

Verification: a test with a fake runner that blocks inside a patch step asserts sync, rollback and rerere forget succeed meanwhile and that the lock is not held then.

### 5. Rebuild-active guard

`internal/wslock` gains a per-workspace guard, independent of the mutex: `BeginRebuild(slug string) (end func(), ok bool)` and `RebuildActive(slug string) bool`. `BeginRebuild` is called by the rebuild while it holds the workspace lock, so there is no gap against archive and reclone, and returns `ok=false` if a guard is already set for that slug. In that case the rebuild returns a retryable error. `end` is idempotent and is called (deferred) after the worktree has been removed on every exit path, so the guard covers the interval from before stale cleanup until after worktree removal.

Archive (`internal/workspace/handlers.go`, `clone_status == "ready"` branch) and reclone (`reclone_handler.go`) call `RebuildActive(slug)` after a successful `TryLock` and, when it is true, release the lock and answer `409` with `error_type: workspace_busy` and the existing message. Behaviour of archive and reclone when no rebuild is active is unchanged. A process crash clears the guard because it is in memory.

Verification: tests assert archive and reclone return `409 workspace_busy` while the guard is set and the lock is free, and succeed after `end()`; and that sync, rollback and rerere forget are not rejected by the guard.

### 6. Snapshotting patch tips

After the patch list is sorted and before the first patch is applied, the rebuild resolves each patch that will be attempted (status not `merged_upstream`, `disabled` or `deleted`) with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` in the trunk runner. From then on only the resulting SHA is used for `git log`, cherry-pick and merge. A branch that does not resolve (error or empty output) is recorded as `skipped` / `branch_not_found` at that point, as today; an empty commit list for the rebase strategy is also `branch_not_found`, as today.

- Rebase strategy: `git log ... <base>...<sha>`.
- Merge strategy: `MergeNoFF(ctx, sha, "Merge branch '<branch name>'")`. The merge commit message names the branch and the SHA.
- `PatchResult` gains `SourceSHA string` with JSON name `source_sha` (omitted when empty), set for every patch that was snapshotted, including ones that then conflicted. It appears in the job result, in the running job's progress, and therefore in the `patch_results` of rebuild API responses. `docs/api.md` and `docs/openapi.yaml` list the new field.

Resolution is limited to `refs/heads/` (a tag or remote-tracking ref of the same name no longer matches), in line with ADR 01's finding that patch branches are only usable as local heads.

### 7. Stale-input follow-up

As the last step before returning, after worktree removal and after the phase-two lock is released, the rebuild checks whether its inputs moved during the run:

- **Patch tips:** for each patch with a snapshot SHA whose status was `success` or `conflict`, resolve `refs/heads/<branch>` again. If any now differs from its snapshot SHA, the patch is stale. Patches skipped for status (`merged_upstream`, `disabled`, `deleted`) are ignored.
- **Upstream base:** re-run `resolveUpstreamBase`. If it differs from the SHA the run used, upstream is stale.

A stale patch tip enqueues a follow-up unless the workspace variable `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH` is `"false"`. A stale upstream enqueues one unless `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` is `"false"`. At most one follow-up is enqueued per run. The check runs for a successful run and for a fail-fast conflict exit (a push that fixes the conflicting patch while the run was applying must not be lost). It does not run on retryable errors, cancellation or other failures.

The follow-up carries the same payload (strategy, fail mode and integration branch as the original) with `SubmittedBy: "system:stale-snapshot"`, a fresh nonce, `Type: "rebuild"`, `Key: <slug>`, and the running job's `GroupKey` (read with `Queue.GetByID(jobID)`, falling back to `FormatGroupKey(slug, payload.IntegrationBranch)`). To make this possible `jobqueue.EnqueueParams` gains `ExcludeJobID string`: when set, the active `(type, key)` duplicate check (both the pre-insert query and the race-recovery query) ignores the job with that ID. The new job is inserted as `queued` and, because it shares the group key, does not start until the current job is finalised. A later push hook or sync enqueue is then deduplicated against the queued follow-up, as intended. With a nil `Queue` (unit tests) or an enqueue error, the rebuild logs a warning and the job outcome is unchanged. A `hub.rebuild.followup` audit event is emitted when a follow-up is enqueued, with `stale_patches` (branch names), `upstream_stale` (bool) and `follow_up_job_id` in metadata.

A residual window remains between the final re-resolution and the job being finalised in which a push or sync enqueue is still deduplicated against the running job. It is tolerated; the final check is placed last to keep it to milliseconds.

Verification: a test pushes to a registered patch branch while a rebuild is blocked mid-application (controllable fake for one step), asserts the run applied the snapshot SHA, the trunk's HEAD moved to the pushed commit, a follow-up job exists in `queued` state with `submitted_by = system:stale-snapshot`, and `hub.rebuild.followup` was emitted. Further tests cover upstream drift, both variables set to `"false"`, and a `jobqueue` test for `ExcludeJobID`.

### 8. Cancellation and crash recovery

On cancellation of the job context during patch application the rebuild discards the worktree (removal with `--force` also discards any in-progress cherry-pick or merge), ends the guard, and returns a retryable `TransientError`. The cleanup uses the non-cancelled context from Requirement 1. A context error from any git call is treated as cancellation and takes this path.

If the hub dies mid-run, nothing needs doing in the trunk. Before creating its worktree, and under the guard, the next rebuild of the workspace removes every directory under `<workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/` (`os.RemoveAll`) and runs `git worktree prune` in the trunk. This replaces `preflightCleanup`.

On startup, before `mergeQueue.Start()` in `cmd/af-hub/main.go`, the hub calls a new `carrypatch.CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees(ctx, workspaceRoot, logger)` that, for every `<workspace_root>/*/rebuild` directory, removes it, runs `git worktree prune` in the matching `trunk` (skipped with a warning if the trunk is missing), and logs each removal. Errors are logged and never prevent startup. Running before the queue starts guarantees no rebuild is concurrently using one of those directories.

Verification: a test creates a registered-but-orphaned worktree directory under `rebuild/` (and a plain stale directory), then asserts the next rebuild succeeds and the directories and registrations are gone; another test covers the startup cleanup function, including a workspace without a trunk.

### 9. Coexistence with go-git, pushes and gc

A `git push` through the hub during patch application updates refs and resets the trunk's working tree exactly as when no rebuild runs (the `TryLock` in `updateHeadSHA` now succeeds, so the reset happens). It does not affect the worktree. A `POST /sync` during patch application fetches upstream and updates `upstream_head_sha`; the running rebuild keeps the base it resolved in phase one, and Requirement 7 ensures the drift produces a follow-up. Objects reachable only from the worktree's HEAD survive any `git gc` because git treats every worktree's HEAD as a root; the rebuild never runs `gc --prune=now` or `reflog expire`.

An integration test with a real repository, while a linked rebuild worktree is registered under the trunk, exercises every go-git path the hub uses on the trunk and asserts each succeeds and leaves the worktree usable: `git.PlainOpen` plus `Worktree().Reset(&git.ResetOptions{Mode: git.HardReset})` (post-push reset), `defaultSyncUpdateLocalRefFn` (sync fast-forward in `internal/workspace/sync_git.go`), `upstream.Fetch`, and `DefaultPushIntegrationFunc` (to a local bare remote). This test is the evidence for the coexistence assumption. If it fails, the design must change before implementation continues.

### 10. Observability, documentation and decision record

Worktree creation and removal, stale worktree cleanup (per-run and startup) and the `_rebuild_temp` migration are logged at info level with workspace slug and path. `hub.rebuild.complete` and `hub.rebuild.fail` are emitted as today. Removal failures are logged as warnings.

Documentation is updated in the same change:

- `docs/api.md` ("Workspace Lock", the `workspace_busy` row, and the 409 rows for sync, rollback, rerere forget, archive, reclone) and `docs/openapi.yaml`: sync, rollback, rerere forget and batch rebase are rejected only during a rebuild's fetch phase and final phase; archive and reclone are rejected for the whole rebuild. Also document `patch_results[].source_sha`.
- `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md`: rewrite the "Rebuild algorithm" steps 3–6 for the worktree flow, state that a rebuild does not change the trunk's checkout, that clones served by the hub during a rebuild see the pre-rebuild integration branch until the run completes, and that a stale patch tip or upstream triggers a follow-up rebuild. Update the lock note near line 1068.
- `docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md`: the two `_rebuild_temp` statements are removed or marked as legacy.
- A new `docs/adr/02-run-rebuilds-with-the-git-cli.md` records the decision to implement the worktree rebuild with the git CLI rather than go-git, including the capability table (worktree add/remove/prune, cherry-pick, non-FF merge, rerere, gc/prune) as reported by go-git v5.19.1's `COMPATIBILITY.md`, and the condition for revisiting it (go-git gaining linked-worktree, cherry-pick, `--no-ff` merge and rerere support, e.g. in v6).

Existing rebuild unit tests that use the fake runner are updated to expect the worktree commands and `update-ref` instead of `checkout -B`, the restore sequence and `branch -f`.

## Design Decisions

1. **One worktree per run, detached, no temporary branch.** A persistent worktree would carry half-finished state between runs and bring back the cleanup problem. A per-run detached worktree makes crash recovery "delete the directory" and leaves nothing in the trunk's ref namespace.
2. **git CLI through `GitRunner`, not go-git.** go-git v5.19.1 has no linked-worktree creation, cherry-pick, non-FF merge or rerere, and re-implementing them would change an algorithm this spec keeps fixed and put `rr-cache` compatibility at risk. Worktree commands sit behind typed methods so this can be revisited.
3. **Split the lock; add a separate guard instead of keeping the lock.** Only the fetch and the final ref/DB phase write shared state. A mutex cannot express "held long, others may proceed", so archive and reclone, which delete the directory, check a flag in `wslock` instead.
4. **Set the guard under the lock, check it under the lock.** Both sides use the workspace mutex around the flag, so archive cannot slip in between the rebuild acquiring the lock and setting the guard.
5. **Rebuild keeps blocking `Lock`; no special "retryable while archive holds the lock" rule.** Waiting for the lock already gives that behaviour, and a vanished workspace fails at the fetch and is retried by the queue as today.
6. **Cleanup uses `context.WithoutCancel` with a timeout.** The existing cleanup silently did nothing on cancellation because it reused the cancelled context; the worktree design depends on removal actually running.
7. **Final ref update uses `update-ref`, not `branch -f`.** `branch -f` refuses a branch checked out in any worktree, including the trunk. `update-ref` always works.
8. **Exception A: hard-reset the trunk when it has the integration branch checked out.** Moving a ref under a checked-out branch would leave the trunk inconsistent; the old restore step covered this case implicitly. The reset runs only in that case, so the common case is untouched.
9. **Exception B: migrate a legacy `_rebuild_temp` once.** A pre-upgrade crash can leave the trunk on that branch with a half-applied pick, and the removed `preflightCleanup` was what dealt with it. The target branch is the workspace branch, then `origin/HEAD`, then a detached HEAD, because the workspace branch may be unset or missing locally.
10. **Snapshot tips as SHAs resolved at `refs/heads/<branch>`.** With the lock released, branch names move. Using SHAs makes the run deterministic and `source_sha` tells the operator what was applied. Limiting to `refs/heads/` matches ADR 01.
11. **Follow-up needs `jobqueue.EnqueueParams.ExcludeJobID`.** The queue dedups on `(type, key)` over `queued` and `running` jobs, so a follow-up enqueued by the running rebuild would be deduplicated against itself. Excluding the caller lets it queue; the shared group key keeps it from starting until the current job finishes.
12. **Follow-up also covers upstream drift.** Carry-patch sync only enqueues when `upstream_head_sha` changes, and a sync during a rebuild now stores the new value, so without a rebuild-side check the new upstream is never rebuilt. The proposal's "next sync catches up" is incorrect. Patch drift honours `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH`; upstream drift honours `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC`.
13. **Follow-up only for patches that were attempted (`success` or `conflict`) and for fail-fast conflict exits.** Disabled, merged and deleted patches take no part in the run, so their movement is irrelevant. A fix pushed during a run that failed on that patch should still be rebuilt. Retryable failures re-snapshot on retry.
14. **One follow-up per run, enqueued last.** Enqueuing after worktree removal and after unlocking keeps the unprotected window (a push or sync deduplicated against the still-running job) to milliseconds.
15. **`MergeNoFF` takes a message.** Merging a SHA would otherwise produce "Merge commit '<sha>'" and lose the branch name from history.
16. **No git-version check added.** The proposal asked for a check against 2.17; `gitcmd.New` already refuses git older than 2.38, which covers `worktree add --detach` and `worktree remove`.
17. **The review PRD erratum is dropped.** The proposal asked to mark `docs/prd/review_2026_09_codebase.md` superseded; that file does not exist in the repository. The `_rebuild_temp` descriptions that do exist are in `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md` and `docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md`, and are updated instead.
18. **`DELETE /workspaces/:slug` is not guarded.** It already requires an archived workspace, and archiving is refused while a rebuild is active.
19. **`source_sha` is additive.** It is the only change to a response shape, is omitted when empty, and gives operators the applied tip.
20. **Sparse checkout is not used.** It would change what cherry-pick sees and complicate rerere; cost is one extra tree per rebuilding workspace, freed at the end of the run or at startup.
21. **Merge jobs stay in the trunk.** They also delete the source branch and run a check command whose working directory is part of the workspace contract. Moving them is a separate change.

## Dependencies

| Spec | Relationship | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| `10_durable_job_queue` | modifies | `EnqueueParams` gains `ExcludeJobID` so a running job can enqueue a follow-up of its own type and key. |
| `11_git_runner` / `14_git_runner_extensions` | modifies | `gitcmd.GitRunner` gains `WorktreeAdd`, `WorktreeRemove`, `WorktreePrune`; the `carrypatch` adapter and interface gain the same plus the `MergeNoFF` message parameter. |
| `16_carry_patch_operations` | modifies | Rebuild executor, progress and result shape (`source_sha`), audit events (`hub.rebuild.followup`), docs. |
| `15_carry_patch_workspace` | depends | Trunk layout, `upstream` remote, rerere config at clone time, `integration_branch`. |
| `13_upstream_sync` | depends | Sync fast-forward path (`sync_git.go`) must keep working while a worktree is registered; reclone is guarded. |
| `05_workspace_checkout` | modifies | Archive answers `409 workspace_busy` while a rebuild is active. |
| `06_git_server` | depends | Post-push `updateHeadSHA` reset must run during patch application and keep working with a registered worktree. |
| `12_merge_operations` | depends | Merge jobs keep using blocking `wslock.Lock` and now run during patch application. |
| `18_hub_audit_query` | modifies | New `hub.rebuild.followup` event type. |

Also needed: `internal/wslock` (guard), `cmd/af-hub/main.go` (startup cleanup), `internal/workspace/reclone_handler.go` (guard check). No new Go modules. `go-git` stays at v5.19.1.

## Verified External API

go-git source is not readable from the module cache in this environment, so the signatures below are taken from calls that already compile in this repository, and the capability claims are taken from the issue's reading of go-git v5.19.1's `COMPATIBILITY.md`. The last item below must be re-checked when the ADR is written.

| Symbol (`github.com/go-git/go-git/v5`) | Use in this repo | Role in this spec |
|---|---|---|
| `git.PlainOpen(path string) (*git.Repository, error)` | `gitserver/handlers.go`, `workspace/sync_git.go`, `carrypatch/wire.go`, `upstream/upstream.go` | Still opens the trunk, unchanged, while a linked worktree is registered (Requirement 9 test). |
| `(*Repository).Worktree() (*git.Worktree, error)` and `(*Worktree).Reset(*git.ResetOptions) error` with `ResetOptions{Commit plumbing.Hash, Mode git.ResetMode}` and `git.HardReset` | post-push reset, sync fast-forward | Must still work on the trunk while the rebuild worktree exists. |
| `(*Repository).PushContext(ctx, *git.PushOptions) error`, `git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate` | `DefaultPushIntegrationFunc` | Runs in the final phase, unchanged. |
| `(*Repository).Storer.SetReference(*plumbing.Reference) error` | `defaultSyncUpdateLocalRefFn` | Unchanged. |
| Linked-worktree creation, `cherry-pick`, `--no-ff` merge, `rerere`, `gc`/`prune` | **NOT FOUND** as go-git features (per the issue's reading of `COMPATIBILITY.md`; `PlainOpenOptions.EnableDotGitCommonDir` only opens an existing linked worktree) | The reason the CLI is used. Not re-verified here. |

Git CLI behaviours this design relies on, to be confirmed by the integration tests rather than assumed: `git worktree add --detach <abs path> <sha>` resolves a relative path against the working directory; `git worktree remove --force` removes a worktree with a conflicted index; `rr-cache` and `rerere.*` config are shared across linked worktrees while `MERGE_RR` is per worktree; `git branch -f` refuses a branch checked out in any worktree while `git update-ref` does not.

## Glossary

- **Exception A**: The case where the trunk's HEAD is the integration branch at the final ref update, so the trunk needs a hard reset to match the new tip.
- **Exception B**: The one-time removal of a legacy _rebuild_temp branch left by a pre-upgrade run, including moving the trunk's HEAD off it.
- **follow-up rebuild**: A rebuild job enqueued by a finished run, with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot, because a patch tip or the upstream base moved during the run.
- **phase one / phase two**: The two lock-holding sections of a rebuild. Phase one covers the upstream fetch, base resolution, legacy migration, stale cleanup and rerere config. Phase two covers the integration-ref update, patch bookkeeping and optional push to origin.
- **rebuild worktree**: A detached linked git worktree created for one rebuild run at <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>. It shares the trunk's objects, refs, configuration and rr-cache but has its own HEAD, index and files.
- **rebuild-active guard**: A per-workspace in-memory flag in internal/wslock, set by BeginRebuild and read by RebuildActive, independent of the wslock mutex. Archive and reclone refuse to run while it is set.
- **rerere**: git's reuse-recorded-resolution feature; its cache rr-cache lives in the common git directory and MERGE_RR is per worktree.
- **snapshot SHA**: The commit SHA that a patch branch resolved to at refs/heads/<branch> when patch application began; it is the only reference to the branch used for the rest of the run.
- **trunk**: The non-bare clone of a workspace at <workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk, shared by the git smart HTTP server, sync, merge jobs, rollback, rerere forget and rebuilds.
- **wslock**: The in-process per-workspace lock in internal/wslock, taken blockingly with Lock by jobs and non-blockingly with TryLock by HTTP handlers.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Worktree lifecycle

**Rationale:** A per-run detached worktree lets patch application proceed without borrowing the trunk checkout and makes crash recovery a matter of deleting a directory.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a rebuild reaches patch application, THE rebuild executor SHALL create a detached worktree with the typed WorktreeAdd call, which runs `git worktree add --detach <path> <upstream base sha>` in the trunk, where <path> is the absolute path (made absolute with filepath.Abs) <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>
   → WorktreeAdd is called once on the trunk runner; the path argument is absolute, equals filepath.Abs('ws/<slug>/rebuild/job-42'); the commit argument is the SHA returned by resolveUpstreamBase; the call is the `git worktree add --detach` form
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner recording typed calls
   - setup: a context carrying job ID 'job-42'
   - setup: WorkspaceRoot is a relative path such as 'ws'
   ```
   h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxWithJobID('job-42'), job); c = mock.calls('WorktreeAdd')[0]; assert filepath.IsAbs(c.path); assert c.path == abs('ws/slug/rebuild/job-42'); assert c.sha == baseSHA
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the job context carries no job ID or the configured WorkspaceRoot is empty, THE rebuild executor SHALL use a random ID in place of the job ID when the job ID is absent, and derive the worktree path from the same parent directory as the trunk path when WorkspaceRoot is empty
   → both worktree paths are <tmp>/<slug>/rebuild/<id> with a non-empty id; the two ids differ; no error is returned because of the empty root
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner
   - setup: a context without a job ID
   - setup: WorkspaceRoot is empty and the trunk path is <tmp>/<slug>/trunk
   ```
   p1 = pathOf(run()); p2 = pathOf(run()); assert dir(p1) == tmp+'/slug/rebuild'; assert base(p1) != '' ; assert p1 != p2
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE rebuild executor SHALL build a second GitRunner with h.NewGitRunner(worktreePath) after the worktree directory exists, run log, rev-parse, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, `diff --diff-filter=U`, `commit --no-edit`, `reset --hard` to the pre-patch HEAD and worktree HEAD reads through it, and use the trunk runner only for fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, the _rebuild_temp migration and the final ref update
   → NewGitRunner is called with the worktree path and the directory exists at that moment; log, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, diff --diff-filter=U, commit --no-edit and HEAD reads are recorded only on the worktree runner; the trunk runner records only fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, update-ref and rev-parse
   Check: unit
   - setup: a RebuildHandler whose NewGitRunner records the path argument and whether the directory existed at call time
   - setup: a mock worktree runner and a mock trunk runner each recording commands
   - setup: one rebase patch and one merge patch
   ```
   assert worktreeRunner.commands ⊇ {log, cherry-pick, merge}; assert trunkRunner.commands ∩ {cherry-pick, merge, log --right-only, commit} == ∅
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE rebuild executor SHALL for any exit path (success, conflict, transient error, early return, cancellation), remove the worktree with WorktreeRemove (`git worktree remove --force <path>`) followed by WorktreePrune (`git worktree prune`), so that `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk and the worktree directory no longer exists
   → <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id> does not exist afterwards; `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk; the outcomes are success, conflict result, TransientError, TransientError respectively
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git repository workspace with an upstream remote and patch branches
   - setup: a conflicting patch branch for the conflict case
   - setup: a failure injected for the transient case and a cancelled context for the cancellation case
   - setup: a mockGitRunner that can inject an error at any step
   ```
   for scenario in [success, conflict, transient, cancel]: run(scenario); assert !exists(wtPath); assert lines(git('worktree list')) == 1
   for step in allSteps+[none,cancel]: run(inject(step)); if mock.added: assert mock.calls.endsWith(['WorktreeRemove','WorktreePrune']) ; assert !exists(path)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF `git worktree remove` fails, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL fall back to os.RemoveAll(path) followed by `git worktree prune`, log the failure at warning level, and leave the job outcome unchanged
   → The job result and status are identical to those of a run whose removal succeeded; a warning log entry naming the slug and path is written; the worktree directory is gone after the fallback
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeRemove returns an error
   - setup: a real temp directory standing in for the worktree path
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   r1 = run(removeOK); r2 = run(removeFails); assert r1 == r2; assert warnLogs contains slug and path; assert !exists(path)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE rebuild executor SHALL run worktree removal and every other cleanup step with a context derived from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and a timeout of at most two minutes, so cleanup still executes after the job context is cancelled
   → ctx.Err() is nil in the cleanup calls; a deadline exists and is no more than two minutes ahead; the worktree removal actually executed
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner that records ctx.Err() and ctx.Deadline() on WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune
   - setup: a job context that is cancelled mid-application
   ```
   assert rec.removeCtxErr == nil; assert rec.deadline - now <= 2*time.Minute
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] THE git runner SHALL provide WorktreeAdd, WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune on gitcmd.GitRunner, the carrypatch.GitRunner interface, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner as the only place worktree commands are spelled, and change MergeNoFF to MergeNoFF(ctx, ref, message string) error where an empty message keeps git's default merge message
   → the worktree is created, listed, removed and pruned; the merge with a message has that message as the commit subject; the merge with an empty message has git's default message; the interface assertion `var _ GitRunner = (*mockGitRunner)(nil)` compiles
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real temporary git repository with two diverging branches
   - setup: gitcmd.GitRunner, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner compiled against the carrypatch.GitRunner interface
   ```
   a.WorktreeAdd(ctx,p,sha); a.WorktreeRemove(ctx,p); a.WorktreePrune(ctx); a.MergeNoFF(ctx,'b',"Merge branch 'b'"); assert subject(HEAD)=="Merge branch 'b'"
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] IF creating the worktree fails, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL stop the run before applying any patch, leave no directory under rebuild/ for this run, release the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
   → HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no integration-ref update or patch bookkeeping has occurred; the trunk HEAD, index and files are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeAdd returns an error
   - setup: a captured audit sink
   - setup: a database with patch rows
   ```
   err = run(); assert err != nil; assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')==0; assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)
   ```

### REQ-2: The trunk is not touched

**Rationale:** The shared trunk checkout serves clones, sync and merge jobs, so a rebuild must neither move it nor leave state in it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] THE rebuild executor SHALL run no `checkout`, `reset`, `cherry-pick`, `merge` or `rebase` through the trunk runner during a rebuild other than those defined by Exception A and Exception B, never create the _rebuild_temp branch, and not contain the functions currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup
   → the trunk runner records none of checkout, reset, cherry-pick, merge, rebase; the branch _rebuild_temp is never created; the source contains no function currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner recording trunk commands
   - setup: no _rebuild_temp branch and the trunk not on the integration branch
   - setup: the rebuild_executor.go source
   ```
   assert trunk.cmds ∩ {checkout,reset,cherry-pick,merge,rebase}==∅; assert !grep('func (currentCheckout|restoreCheckout|preflightCleanup)')
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE rebuild executor SHALL for any rebuild that ends in success, fail-fast conflict, continue-mode conflict or cancellation, leave the trunk's `git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain` output and the contents of a tracked sample file identical to their values before the run, except under Exception A and Exception B
   → `git symbolic-ref HEAD` is identical to before; `git rev-parse HEAD` is identical to before; `git status --porcelain` output is identical to before; the sample file bytes are identical to before
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is checked out on a non-integration branch with a tracked sample file
   - setup: patch branches including a conflicting one
   - setup: a real git workspace with a trunk checked out on a branch other than the integration branch
   ```
   before = snap(trunk); run(scenario); assert snap(trunk) == before
   for cfg in gen(): before=snap(trunk); run(cfg); assert snap(trunk)==before
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN patch application finishes and phase two begins, THE rebuild executor SHALL force-update the integration branch to the worktree's final HEAD SHA with `git update-ref refs/heads/<integration> <sha>` using the existing UpdateRef method, never using `branch -f` and never checking the integration branch out
   → UpdateRef is called on the trunk runner with refs/heads/<integration> and 'abc123'; no `branch -f` or checkout of the integration branch is recorded
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner whose worktree HEAD returns SHA 'abc123'
   ```
   assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')[0] == ('refs/heads/'+integ,'abc123'); assert no call has args ['branch','-f',...]
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN phase two holds the workspace lock, THE rebuild executor SHALL read the previous integration head with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration>` immediately before the ref update and record it as previous_integration_head_sha, leaving it empty when the branch does not exist
   → rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration> immediately precedes UpdateRef while the lock is held; previous_integration_head_sha is 'old1' in the first case and empty in the second
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner recording call order and lock state
   - setup: two cases: the integration branch exists at SHA 'old1' and it does not exist
   ```
   assert order == [rev-parse --verify, UpdateRef]; assert lockHeld at both; assert result.prev == 'old1' / ''
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN the ref update has been made under the final lock and the trunk's HEAD is the symbolic ref of the integration branch (Exception A), THE rebuild executor SHALL run `reset --hard HEAD` in the trunk so the index and files match the new tip, and log this at info level; in every other case run no reset in the trunk
   → case 1: after the run the trunk's files and index match the new integration tip, `git status --porcelain` is empty, and an info log entry records the reset; case 2: no reset is run in the trunk and the trunk is unchanged
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git workspace
   - setup: case 1: the trunk has the integration branch checked out
   - setup: case 2: the trunk is on another branch
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   case1: assert git(trunk,'rev-parse HEAD')==newTip; assert status==''; assert infoLog('reset'); case2: assert trunkCmds ∩ {reset}==∅
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN phase one runs and a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp exists (Exception B), THE rebuild executor SHALL delete that branch and log at info level that it was removed
   → After the run `git show-ref refs/heads/_rebuild_temp` finds nothing and a log entry with the slug records the removal
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is on another branch
   - setup: a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   run(); assert exitCode(git('show-ref','refs/heads/_rebuild_temp'))!=0; assert infoLog contains slug
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] WHEN the _rebuild_temp migration runs and the trunk's HEAD is on _rebuild_temp and any cherry-pick, merge or rebase may be in progress, THE rebuild executor SHALL abort any in-progress cherry-pick, merge or rebase on a best-effort basis, then move HEAD with `checkout --force <branch>` where <branch> is workspaceBranch if it exists as a local branch, else the short name of refs/remotes/origin/HEAD if that exists locally, else run `checkout --detach --force` and log a warning, before deleting _rebuild_temp
   → the in-progress operation is aborted; variant 1: trunk HEAD is on workspaceBranch; variant 2: trunk HEAD is on the short name of origin/HEAD; variant 3: trunk HEAD is detached and a warning is logged; _rebuild_temp no longer exists in all variants
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is on _rebuild_temp with an in-progress conflicted cherry-pick
   - setup: three variants: workspaceBranch exists locally; it is unset but refs/remotes/origin/HEAD resolves to a local branch; neither exists
   ```
   for v in variants: setup(v); run(); assert symbolicRef(trunk)==expected(v); assert !branchExists('_rebuild_temp')
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] IF the `update-ref` of the integration branch fails, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL stop phase two before any soft-deletion, compaction or push, release the lock, and emit hub.rebuild.fail
   → HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no patch rows are changed by this run; the lock is free afterwards
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner whose UpdateRef fails
   - setup: a database with merged_upstream and active patches and a PushIntegration spy
   ```
   err=run(); assert err!=nil; assert rowsUnchanged(); assert push.calls==0; assert tryLock(slug)
   ```

### REQ-3: Rerere across worktrees

**Rationale:** Conflict resolutions recorded by the hub's rebuilds must keep replaying and stay visible to the rerere endpoints even though patches are applied in a linked worktree.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] THE rebuild executor SHALL set rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true in the repository-level config with the trunk runner before creating the worktree, and not enable extensions.worktreeConfig
   → config rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true are issued on the trunk runner before WorktreeAdd; no config call mentions extensions.worktreeConfig
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mockGitRunner recording call order
   ```
   assert idx('config rerere.enabled true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert idx('config rerere.autoupdate true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert none(args contains 'worktreeConfig')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a rebuild meets a conflict whose resolution an earlier rebuild recorded in its worktree, THE rebuild executor SHALL replay the recorded resolution from the shared rr-cache so the patch is applied without a reported conflict
   → the conflicting patch is reported as success rather than conflict; the result tree contains the recorded resolution
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real git workspace with two patch branches that conflict on the same hunk
   - setup: a first rebuild that conflicts, after which the conflict is resolved in its worktree and recorded in rr-cache
   ```
   run1(); resolveAndRecord(); r=run2(); assert r.patch[1].status=='success'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE rerere endpoints SHALL for any resolution recorded in a rebuild worktree, list it in GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache and remove it with DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rerere/*, with the entry absent from a following GET
   → the first GET is 200 and lists the entry; DELETE succeeds; the second GET does not list the entry and the rr-cache directory for it is gone from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace with an HTTP router wired to the rerere handlers
   - setup: one resolution recorded by a rebuild worktree into the common rr-cache
   - setup: a real workspace and rerere handlers
   ```
   assert entry in get().entries; assert delete(entry).status==200; assert entry not in get().entries
   for set,order in gen(): record(set); for e in order: delete(e); assert get() == set - deleted
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a rebuild worktree is discarded while a conflict is in progress and MERGE_RR is populated, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL leave the shared rr-cache and the endpoints' read of <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR unaffected
   → GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere returns 200 with the entries recorded before the discard, and <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR holds no entry from the discarded worktree
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace with one previously recorded resolution
   - setup: a rebuild that stops on a conflict so MERGE_RR is populated in the worktree
   ```
   assert get().status==200; assert entriesBefore ⊆ get().entries; assert read(trunk/.git/MERGE_RR)==''
   ```

### REQ-4: Lock phases

**Rationale:** Only the fetch and the final ref and database update write shared state, so holding the workspace lock for patch application blocks sync, rollback and merge jobs for no benefit.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a rebuild job starts, THE rebuild executor SHALL resolve upstream credentials first, then take the blocking wslock.Lock(slug), and under that lock call BeginRebuild(slug)
   → order is credentials, Lock, BeginRebuild; BeginRebuild observed the lock held
   Check: unit
   - setup: spies for credential resolution, wslock.Lock and BeginRebuild recording order and lock state
   ```
   assert order==['creds','Lock','BeginRebuild']; assert lockHeldDuring(BeginRebuild)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF resolving upstream credentials fails, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL return a retryable TransientError before taking the lock or setting the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
   → HandleRebuildJob returns an error of type TransientError; the lock is free and RebuildActive(slug) is false
   Check: unit
   - setup: credential resolution returning an error
   - setup: a captured audit sink
   ```
   err=run(); var te *TransientError; assert errors.As(err,&te); assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE rebuild executor SHALL perform in phase one under the lock, in this order, the upstream fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, the _rebuild_temp migration, stale worktree cleanup and rerere config, and then release the lock
   → order is fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, _rebuild_temp migration, stale cleanup, rerere config; the lock is held for every step and released before WorktreeAdd
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mock runner and spies recording order and lock state
   ```
   assert order==[fetch,newRunner,resolveBase,migrate,staleCleanup,rerereConfig]; assert allLocked; assert !locked(at WorktreeAdd)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHILE the rebuild is creating the worktree, listing patches, snapshotting tips or applying patches, THE rebuild executor SHALL hold no wslock lock, so that POST /sync, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase and merge jobs for the same workspace acquire the lock and proceed
   → TryLock(slug) succeeds while blocked; sync responds with its normal success status, not 409 workspace_busy, and updates upstream_head_sha; rollback and rerere forget succeed; the rebuild keeps the base SHA resolved in phase one and completes
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake runner that blocks inside a cherry-pick until released
   - setup: real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
   - setup: the rebuild started in a goroutine
   ```
   go run(); <-blocked; assert tryLock(slug); assert post('/sync').status==200; assert rollback().status==200; assert forget().status==200; release()
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] THE rebuild executor SHALL re-acquire wslock.Lock(slug) for phase two, perform in it the previous-head read, the integration-ref update, soft-deletion of merged_upstream patches, position compaction and the optional PushIntegration to origin, and release the lock afterwards
   → Lock is acquired a second time after patch application; previous-head read, UpdateRef, soft-deletion, compaction and PushIntegration all happen with the lock held in that order; the lock is released afterwards
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mock runner, a PushIntegration spy and a database with merged_upstream patches
   ```
   assert order==[lock,readPrev,updateRef,softDelete,compact,push,unlock]
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] THE rebuild executor SHALL for any early return in phase one or phase two, release the workspace lock, and perform worktree creation, patch application and worktree removal outside any lock
   → tryLock(slug) succeeds after HandleRebuildJob returns; WorktreeAdd, patch application and WorktreeRemove never run while the lock is held
   Check: property
   - setup: a mock runner that can fail at any step
   ```
   for step in allSteps: run(failAt(step)); assert tryLock(slug); assert !lockedDuring(worktree ops)
   ```
1. [REQ-4.7] WHEN a rollback of the integration branch completes while patches are being applied, THE rebuild executor SHALL overwrite the rolled-back value with its own update-ref in phase two and record in previous_integration_head_sha the value read at phase two, with rollback and the final update serialised by the lock
   → After the run the integration branch equals the rebuild's final HEAD SHA and previous_integration_head_sha equals the rolled-back SHA
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace whose integration branch is at SHA 'A'
   - setup: a rebuild blocked mid-application
   - setup: a rollback target SHA 'R'
   ```
   rollback('R'); release(); assert rev('integration')==finalSHA; assert result.prev=='R'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.8] THE rebuild executor SHALL after phase two, remove the worktree, run the stale-input check, emit hub.rebuild.complete, end the guard and return, in that order
   → order is WorktreeRemove, stale check, hub.rebuild.complete, end guard; RebuildActive(slug) is true until the complete event
   Check: unit
   - setup: spies recording order for WorktreeRemove, stale-input check, audit emit and the end() call
   ```
   assert order==[remove,staleCheck,emit('hub.rebuild.complete'),end]
   ```

### REQ-5: Rebuild-active guard

**Rationale:** Archive and reclone delete the directory the worktree lives in, and a mutex that is not held during patch application cannot stop them.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE wslock SHALL provide BeginRebuild(slug string) (end func(), ok bool) and RebuildActive(slug string) bool as a per-workspace flag independent of the mutex, and clear the flag on process exit because it is held only in memory
   → RebuildActive('a') is true after BeginRebuild and Lock/TryLock behaviour is unaffected; RebuildActive('a') is false after the first end(); the second end() does not clear a guard set later by another run
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fresh wslock instance
   ```
   end,ok=BeginRebuild('a'); assert ok&&RebuildActive('a'); assert TryLock('a'); end(); assert !Active; _,ok2=Begin('a'); end(); assert Active('a')
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF BeginRebuild is called for a slug whose guard is already set, THEN THE wslock SHALL return ok=false without changing the existing guard, and make the rebuild return a retryable error
   → BeginRebuild returns (nil-safe end, false); the existing guard stays set; HandleRebuildJob returns a retryable error and the job is retried by the queue
   Check: unit
   - setup: a guard already set for slug 'a'
   ```
   end,ok=Begin('a'); assert !ok; end(); assert Active('a'); err=run(); assert isTransient(err); assert tryLock('a')
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] THE wslock SHALL make the end function returned by BeginRebuild idempotent, so a second call leaves a guard set later by another run untouched
   Check: same as REQ-5.1
1. [REQ-5.4] THE rebuild executor SHALL hold the guard from before stale worktree cleanup until after worktree removal on every exit path, calling end through defer
   → RebuildActive is true at stale cleanup and after WorktreeRemove completes; RebuildActive is false after HandleRebuildJob returns in all scenarios
   Check: unit
   - setup: spies observing RebuildActive at stale cleanup, WorktreeAdd and WorktreeRemove
   - setup: success, patch-conflict and error scenarios
   ```
   for s in scenarios: run(s); assert activeAt('staleCleanup') && activeAt('afterRemove'); assert !Active(slug)
   ```
1. [REQ-5.5] WHEN an archive request reaches the clone_status == "ready" branch, TryLock succeeds and RebuildActive(slug) is true, THE archive handler SHALL release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the workspace is not archived and the lock is free
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace and the real archive handler
   - setup: wslock guard set via BeginRebuild with the mutex free
   ```
   BeginRebuild(slug); r=archive(); assert r.status==409; assert r.json.error_type=='workspace_busy'; assert !isArchived(slug); assert tryLock(slug)
   ```
1. [REQ-5.6] WHEN a reclone request obtains TryLock and RebuildActive(slug) is true, THE reclone handler SHALL release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the clone directory is untouched and the lock is free
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace with a trunk directory and the real reclone handler
   - setup: the guard set and the mutex free
   ```
   BeginRebuild(slug); r=reclone(); assert r.status==409; assert exists(trunk/marker); assert tryLock(slug)
   ```
1. [REQ-5.7] WHILE no rebuild is active for the workspace and the guard has been ended, THE archive and reclone handlers SHALL behave exactly as before this change, so archive and reclone succeed under the same conditions as without the guard
   → archive succeeds with its normal success status and the workspace is archived; reclone is accepted with its normal success status
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace, a guard set then ended with end()
   ```
   end,_=Begin(slug); end(); assert archive().status==200; assert reclone(other).status==202
   ```
1. [REQ-5.8] WHILE the guard is set and the lock is free, THE sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers SHALL not consult the guard and accept their requests
   → none of them returns 409 workspace_busy; each returns its normal success status
   Check: integration
   - setup: the guard set for the workspace and the mutex free
   - setup: real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
   ```
   BeginRebuild(slug); for ep in [sync,rollback,forget]: assert ep().status != 409
   ```

### REQ-6: Snapshotting patch tips

**Rationale:** With the lock released during application, branch names can move, so applying fixed SHAs makes the run deterministic and tells the operator exactly what was applied.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN the patch list is sorted and before the first patch is applied, THE rebuild executor SHALL resolve every patch whose status is not merged_upstream, disabled or deleted with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` in the trunk runner and use only the resulting SHA for `git log`, cherry-pick and merge from then on
   → rev-parse --verify is called only for non-merged_upstream/disabled/deleted patches, on the trunk runner, with refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}; the resolution happens after sorting and before the first patch application; log, cherry-pick and merge arguments contain the snapshot SHA and never the branch name
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mock trunk runner returning SHAs per branch
   - setup: patches with statuses active, merged_upstream, disabled and deleted
   - setup: a branch that moves in the mock after the snapshot
   ```
   assert trunk.calls('rev-parse --verify')==activeBranches; assert none(worktree.args contains branchName)
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN a patch uses the rebase strategy, THE rebuild executor SHALL list its commits with `git log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick <base>...<snapshot sha>` in the worktree
   → the worktree runner receives log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick base1...sha1
   Check: unit
   - setup: a rebase-strategy patch with snapshot SHA 'sha1' and base 'base1'
   - setup: a mock worktree runner
   ```
   assert worktree.args('log')==['log','--reverse','--no-merges','--right-only','--cherry-pick','base1...sha1']
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN a patch uses the merge strategy, THE rebuild executor SHALL call MergeNoFF(ctx, <snapshot sha>, "Merge branch '<branch name>'") in the worktree
   → The resulting merge commit message contains the branch name
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace with a merge-strategy patch branch 'feature/x'
   ```
   run(); assert git('log -1 --format=%B integration') contains 'feature/x'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] IF a patch branch's rev-parse fails or returns empty output, or the rebase strategy yields an empty commit list, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL record the patch as skipped with reason branch_not_found and continue with the remaining patches
   → patch_results contains an entry with status skipped and reason branch_not_found for that patch; the run does not fail because of it
   Check: unit
   - setup: three patches: rev-parse errors, rev-parse returns empty output, and a rebase patch whose log is empty
   - setup: a fourth healthy patch after them
   ```
   r,err=run(); assert err==nil; assert r.patches[0..2] all skipped/branch_not_found; assert r.patches[3].status=='success'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] IF a tag or remote-tracking ref has the patch's name but no refs/heads/<branch> exists, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL treat the branch as not found
   → The patch is recorded as skipped with reason branch_not_found
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace where tag 'p1' and refs/remotes/origin/p2 exist but no refs/heads/p1 or refs/heads/p2
   ```
   r=run(); assert r.patches[p1]==('skipped','branch_not_found'); assert r.patches[p2]==('skipped','branch_not_found')
   ```
1. [REQ-6.6] THE rebuild executor SHALL add PatchResult.SourceSHA with JSON name source_sha, omitted when empty, set for every snapshotted patch including those that then conflicted, and carry it in the job result, in the running job's progress and in the patch_results of rebuild API responses
   → success and conflict patches carry their snapshot SHA in source_sha; the disabled patch's JSON has no source_sha key; the running job's progress snapshots include source_sha; the API response patch_results include source_sha
   Check: unit
   - setup: a run with one success patch, one conflict patch (continue mode) and one disabled patch
   - setup: a progress recorder and the rebuild API response encoder
   ```
   assert json(r.patches[0]).source_sha==sha0; assert 'source_sha' not in json(r.patches[2]); assert progress.last.patches[0].source_sha==sha0
   ```
1. [REQ-6.7] THE rebuild executor SHALL for any patch branch that moves after its snapshot, apply exactly the commits reachable from the snapshot SHA and report that SHA as source_sha
   → the applied commits equal those reachable from the snapshot SHA only; source_sha equals the snapshot SHA
   Check: property
   - setup: a real workspace and a rebuild blocked after snapshotting
   ```
   for mv in gen(): snapshot; apply(mv); assert appliedCommits==log(base...snap); assert result.source_sha==snap
   ```

### REQ-7: Stale-input follow-up

**Rationale:** Releasing the lock during application lets a push or a sync land mid-run, and without a rebuild-side check the change would never be rebuilt because sync only enqueues when upstream_head_sha changes.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a run ends in success or in a fail-fast conflict, after worktree removal and after the phase-two lock is released, THE rebuild executor SHALL re-resolve refs/heads/<branch> for each patch with a snapshot SHA and status success or conflict, mark a patch stale if the result differs from its snapshot SHA, ignore patches skipped for merged_upstream, disabled or deleted, and re-run resolveUpstreamBase and mark upstream stale if it differs from the SHA the run used
   → the check runs after WorktreeRemove and with the lock free; only the success and conflict patches are marked stale; the merged_upstream patch is ignored; upstream is marked stale; the check also runs in the fail-fast conflict exit
   Check: unit
   - setup: a mock runner where success and conflict patch branches re-resolve to new SHAs, and a merged_upstream patch branch also moved
   - setup: resolveUpstreamBase returning a different SHA the second time
   - setup: a fail-fast conflict variant
   ```
   assert order==[unlock,remove,staleCheck]; assert stale.patches==['p1','p2']; assert stale.upstream
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF a run ends with a retryable error, cancellation or any failure other than a fail-fast conflict, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL skip the stale-input check and enqueue no follow-up
   → No job with submitted_by system:stale-snapshot exists after the run and no hub.rebuild.followup event is emitted
   Check: unit
   - setup: moved patch tips and upstream
   - setup: a real in-memory jobqueue and audit sink
   ```
   for s in [transient,cancel,otherFail]: run(s); assert queue.countBySubmitter('system:stale-snapshot')==0; assert audit.none('hub.rebuild.followup')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN at least one patch is stale and the workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is not "false", THE rebuild executor SHALL enqueue one follow-up rebuild, and enqueue none when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH is "false"
   → with the variable unset exactly one follow-up is enqueued; with 'false' none is enqueued
   Check: unit
   - setup: a run whose patch tip moved during the run
   - setup: workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH unset, then 'false'
   ```
   assert queue.count('system:stale-snapshot')==1 (unset); ==0 ('false')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] WHEN the upstream base is stale and the workspace variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not "false", THE rebuild executor SHALL enqueue one follow-up rebuild, and enqueue none when AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false"
   → with the variable unset exactly one follow-up is enqueued; with 'false' none is enqueued; AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH='false' alone does not suppress an upstream follow-up
   Check: unit
   - setup: a run during which resolveUpstreamBase changes
   - setup: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset, then 'false'
   ```
   assert count==1 (unset); ==0 (SYNC=false); ==1 (PUSH=false only)
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] THE rebuild executor SHALL enqueue at most one follow-up per run, carrying the same strategy, fail mode and integration branch as the original, SubmittedBy "system:stale-snapshot", a fresh nonce, Type "rebuild", Key <slug> and the running job's GroupKey read with Queue.GetByID(jobID), falling back to FormatGroupKey(slug, payload.IntegrationBranch)
   → The new job is stored with status queued and does not start before the current job is finalised
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real jobqueue with a running rebuild job whose GroupKey is 'g1'
   - setup: both a stale patch and a stale upstream
   ```
   fu=queue.listQueued(); assert len(fu)==1; assert fu[0].GroupKey=='g1'; assert fu[0].Payload.nonce != orig.nonce; assert fu[0].Status=='queued'
   ```
1. [REQ-7.6] THE jobqueue SHALL add EnqueueParams.ExcludeJobID so that, when set, both the pre-insert active (type, key) duplicate query and the race-recovery query ignore the job with that ID, and leave the dedup behaviour unchanged when it is empty
   → empty ExcludeJobID returns the existing job J as a duplicate; ExcludeJobID=J inserts a new queued job; the race-recovery query also ignores J; a different active duplicate (not J) is still deduplicated
   Check: unit
   - setup: a real jobqueue database with a running job J of type 'rebuild' key 'k'
   - setup: a race-recovery scenario where the insert hits the unique index
   ```
   assert Enqueue(p).ID==J; assert Enqueue(p+Exclude J).ID != J
   ```
1. [REQ-7.7] WHEN a follow-up rebuild is enqueued, THE rebuild executor SHALL emit the audit event hub.rebuild.followup, registered as a new event type for audit queries, with metadata stale_patches (branch names), upstream_stale (bool) and follow_up_job_id
   → one hub.rebuild.followup event is emitted; metadata stale_patches is ['a','b'], upstream_stale is true, follow_up_job_id equals the new job's ID; audit queries accept hub.rebuild.followup as an event type
   Check: unit
   - setup: a captured audit sink and the audit query event-type registry
   - setup: a run with stale patches 'a' and 'b' and upstream stale
   ```
   ev=audit.last(); assert ev.type=='hub.rebuild.followup'; assert ev.meta.follow_up_job_id==fu.ID; assert registry.has('hub.rebuild.followup')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.8] IF the Queue is nil or the follow-up enqueue returns an error, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL log a warning and leave the job outcome unchanged
   → HandleRebuildJob returns the same result and error as without the stale check, and a warning log entry is written
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stale run
   - setup: case 1: Queue is nil; case 2: enqueue returns an error
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   r,err=run(case); assert (r,err)==baseline; assert warnLog count>=1
   ```

### REQ-8: Cancellation and crash recovery

**Rationale:** Cleanup that reuses a cancelled context silently does nothing, and a crash must not leave state in the trunk or block later rebuilds.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] IF the job context is cancelled during patch application or a git call returns a context error, THEN THE rebuild executor SHALL discard the worktree with the non-cancelled cleanup context (the forced removal also discards any in-progress cherry-pick or merge), end the guard and return a retryable TransientError
   → HandleRebuildJob returns a TransientError; the worktree directory and registration are gone; RebuildActive(slug) is false; trunk HEAD, index and files are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake runner that cancels the job context inside a cherry-pick and returns ctx.Err()
   - setup: a real or mock trunk with HEAD, index and files recorded
   ```
   err=run(); assert isTransient(err); assert !exists(wt); assert !Active(slug); assert snap(trunk)==before
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN a rebuild runs phase one under the guard and before creating its worktree, THE rebuild executor SHALL remove every directory under <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/ with os.RemoveAll and run `git worktree prune` in the trunk, replacing preflightCleanup, and log each removal at info level
   → both directories are removed; WorktreePrune is called on the trunk runner before WorktreeAdd; RebuildActive was true during the cleanup; an info log entry per removal carries the slug and path
   Check: unit
   - setup: two stale directories under <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/
   - setup: a mock trunk runner and a captured logger
   ```
   assert !exists(d1)&&!exists(d2); assert idx(Prune)<idx(WorktreeAdd); assert infoLogs==2
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN the hub starts, before mergeQueue.Start() in cmd/af-hub/main.go, THE hub SHALL call carrypatch.CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees(ctx, workspaceRoot, logger), which removes every <workspace_root>/*/rebuild directory, runs `git worktree prune` in the matching trunk and logs each removal at info level
   → both rebuild directories are gone and `git worktree list` in each trunk shows only the trunk; an info log entry per removal carries the slug and path; main.go calls the function before mergeQueue.Start()
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace root with two workspaces, each with a real trunk with a registered worktree under rebuild/
   - setup: the source of cmd/af-hub/main.go
   ```
   CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees(ctx,root,l); assert !exists(root/a/rebuild); assert lines(git(a/trunk,'worktree list'))==1; assert idx(src,'CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees')<idx(src,'mergeQueue.Start()')
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] IF a workspace has a rebuild directory but its trunk directory is missing, THEN THE CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees SHALL skip the prune for that workspace, log a warning and continue with the remaining workspaces
   → The function returns without panicking; other workspaces are still cleaned; the rebuild directory of the trunkless workspace is removed
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace root with workspace 'a' having rebuild/ but no trunk and workspace 'b' having rebuild/ and a trunk
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   assert noPanic(call); assert warn contains 'a'; assert !exists(a/rebuild)&&!exists(b/rebuild)
   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] IF removing a directory or pruning fails during startup cleanup, THEN THE CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees SHALL log the error and continue, never returning a failure that stops hub startup
   → Hub startup proceeds to mergeQueue.Start(); an error-level or warning-level log entry names the slug and path
   Check: unit
   - setup: a rebuild directory that cannot be removed (read-only parent) and a trunk where prune fails
   - setup: a captured logger
   ```
   CleanupStaleRebuildWorktrees(...); assert logs.level>=Warn contains slug and path; assert processed(otherWorkspace)
   ```
1. [REQ-8.6] WHEN a previous run crashed leaving a registered-but-orphaned worktree directory and a plain stale directory under rebuild/, THE rebuild executor SHALL remove both directories and their worktree registrations before creating the new worktree, so the next rebuild succeeds
   → After the run `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk and the rebuild/ directory contains no stale entries
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real workspace
   - setup: a registered worktree under rebuild/ whose directory was deleted or orphaned, and a plain unregistered stale directory under rebuild/
   ```
   r,err=run(); assert err==nil; assert lines(git('worktree list'))==1; assert readdir(rebuild)==[]
   ```

### REQ-9: Coexistence with go-git, pushes and gc

**Rationale:** The hub uses go-git on the trunk while a linked worktree is registered, and the design is only valid if those paths keep working.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN a git push through the hub completes while patches are being applied, THE git server SHALL update refs and run the go-git hard reset of the trunk working tree through updateHeadSHA, whose TryLock succeeds, leaving the rebuild worktree's HEAD, index and files unchanged
   → the ref is updated; updateHeadSHA's TryLock succeeds and the trunk's working tree is hard-reset (trunk HEAD moved to the pushed commit when it is the checked-out branch); the rebuild worktree's HEAD, index and files are unchanged
   Check: integration
